views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the already-announced 10% List 4 tariffs as scheduled leverage, but do not add new tariff tranches, raise the 10% rate, or expand entity-list/currency measures before the September talks. Send Lighthizer and Mnuchin back to the table to reopen purchases and structural text; treat any delay or narrowing of List 4 as something China must earn with verifiable farm buying and enforceable IP/enforcement language. Huawei stays on the Entity List. Unilateral rollback now would reward the yuan break and the farm cutoff; another escalation now would land on U.S. consumers and farmers first.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is elevated but not existential. After the Osaka pause (no new tariffs "for the time being"), Shanghai produced little progress and the U.S. announced 10% on the remaining ~$300B effective Sept 1 — the first tranche that is heavily consumer goods (apparel, footwear, electronics). Markets treated that as a growth shock: the Dow swung hundreds of points, oil had its steepest one-day drop in years, VIX spiked to 24.59 on Aug 5, the 10-year yield collapsed to 1.71% (from ~2.65% in February), and Michigan sentiment fell from 98.4 in July to 89.8 in August. China then let CNY through 7 (7.06 on Aug 7) and suspended U.S. agricultural purchases; the Farm Bureau called it a "body blow," with soybean shipments already down from 27.5mt to 10.1mt year-to-date. That is real exposure of a key export sector plus a pending household tax, which sits below the +0.5 "high" anchor because U.S. industrial production is still roughly flat, CPI is contained, and List 4 is not yet in force. The manipulator designation (first since 1994) is mostly symbolic — IMF referral, no immediate sanctions — but it confirms the dispute has spilled into FX. Action stays at 0 / negotiate because the U.S. still has unused leverage (Sept 1 clock, Huawei licenses, IMF track) while further escalation would be self-harming: List 4 is already the consumer hit, China might answer with rarer-earth or broader farm tariffs, and September talks remain on the calendar. Rolling back without a matching Chinese offer would also be a mistake — Beijing just walked purchase commitments and used the exchange rate to blunt existing 25% duties. Hold the line that is already drawn; bargain against it.
key_factors: List 4 (10% on remaining ~$300B consumer goods) announced Aug 1, effective Sept 1, not yet in force
China suspended U.S. farm purchases and threatened extra ag tariffs after calling List 4 a violation of the Osaka consensus
CNY broke 7; Treasury labeled China a currency manipulator (first since 1994) — mostly symbolic but FX now in the fight
U.S. financial/sentiment stress: 10Y 1.71%, VIX 24.59 peak, UMCSENT 89.8, oil ~$51
Shanghai talks failed; September Washington round still scheduled
U.S. goods exports to China weak; China IP and merchandise exports also slowing — both sides taking damage
Huawei Entity List remains the principal non-tariff lever; do not spend it cheaply

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs "for the time being."
U.S. consumer sentiment fell to 89.8 on 2019-08-01 from 98.4 in July (−8.6 points).
10-year Treasury yield 1.71% on 2019-08-07, down 0.94pp (−35%) over the window.
VIX closed 24.59 on 2019-08-05 and 19.49 on 2019-08-07 after the List 4/CNY shock.
CNY/USD 7.0592 on 2019-08-07 after breaking 7 on Aug 5.
U.S. goods exports to China latest $9.4B, down ~11% over the 180-day window.
List 4 hits consumer goods; Dow swung >450 points; oil plunged ~8%; analysts flagged a larger hit to U.S. growth and inflation than prior rounds.
China suspended U.S. agricultural purchases; Farm Bureau called it a body blow; U.S. soybean exports 10.1mt vs 27.5mt a year earlier.
Treasury determined China is a currency manipulator and will engage the IMF; cited concrete steps to devalue while holding large reserves.
